story.title: Riyadh Airport Set to Reopen After Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia
story.summary: Riyadh's international airport is scheduled to reopen after a two-week closure due to repeated attacks from Yemen's Houthis. The airport had suspended operations following strikes targeting the Saudi capital.

event_overview.title: About Yemen Conflict
event_overview.subject: Yemen Conflict
event_overview.summary: The Yemen conflict is a protracted political and armed struggle centered on the Houthi movement (Ansar Allah), Yemen’s internationally recognized government and other Yemeni armed and political actors. It intensified after the Houthis seized Sana’a in 2014 and became regionalized when a Saudi-led coalition intervened in 2015; United Nations-led efforts have sought a negotiated, Yemeni-led settlement.

facts.label: Origins and escalation
facts.value: The present phase escalated in mid-2014, when conflict between government forces, the Houthis and other armed groups intensified; Houthi forces and allied military units took Sana’a in September 2014.

facts.label: Regional intervention
facts.value: A coalition led by Saudi Arabia intervened militarily on 26 March 2015 at the request of then-President Abd Rabbuh Mansur Hadi, transforming the conflict into a regionalized war.

facts.label: Main conflict setting
facts.value: The conflict is principally within Yemen, but it has also involved cross-border hostilities and regional actors; the UN describes it as involving the Houthis, government forces and other armed groups, with consequences for the wider region.

facts.label: UN peace process
facts.value: The Office of the UN Special Envoy for Yemen was established in 2012 to support a Yemeni political transition and has continued to mediate toward a nationwide ceasefire and inclusive political process. A UN-brokered truce began on 2 April 2022, was extended twice, and expired on 2 October 2022.

facts.label: International legal and monitoring frame
facts.value: UN Security Council resolution 2452, adopted on 16 January 2019, established the UN Mission to Support the Hudaydah Agreement (UNMHA) to help implement the Stockholm Agreement’s arrangements for Hudaydah, Salif and Ras Issa ports, including ceasefire monitoring, redeployments and mine action.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers specific developments involving Houthi attacks affecting civilian aviation or critical infrastructure and related airport operations; it does not attempt to cover the full military, political, humanitarian or peace-process history of the Yemen conflict.

explore_lenses.label: Why is the reopening only partial?
explore_lenses.title: Service is resuming under constraints
explore_lenses.summary: The airport has reopened terminals rather than returned immediately to normal operations, reflecting both damage and continuing security risks. The practical effect is limited capacity and uncertain airline availability.

claims.text: King Khalid International Airport assigned Terminal 1 to domestic flights and Terminal 2 to international flights operated by Saudi national carriers, effective October 25.
Reuters reported that flight-tracking data showed little traffic after the partial reopening, despite the airport announcement.
The airport advised passengers with confirmed bookings to check directly with their airline before travelling, indicating that published schedules may not reliably reflect operations.

The airport advised passengers with confirmed bookings to check directly with their airline before travelling, indicating that published schedules may not reliably reflect operations.
explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: Available reporting does not establish when all terminals or the full range of international carriers will resume normal service.

explore_lenses.label: How did the Riyadh shutdown unfold?
explore_lenses.title: Repeated strikes disrupted the airport
explore_lenses.summary: The closure followed a sequence of attacks in early October, not a single isolated incident. Saudi aviation authorities documented damage and casualties, while later reporting described continued attacks through the reopening date.

claims.text: Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said attacks on October 8 targeted airport facilities and a Saudia aircraft, killing three Saudi citizens, injuring others, and causing material damage.
The authority reported a further attack on October 11 that caused injuries and prompted continued assessment of damage and facility safety with security agencies.
Reuters reported that the Saudi-led coalition said Houthis carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and October 11.

Associated Press reported that strikes in early October hit a complex housing two terminals, killing 17 people and wounding more than 330; this aggregate differs from some earlier official incident-by-incident accounts.

explore_lenses.label: What does reopening mean for safety?
explore_lenses.title: Flights resume amid active threats
explore_lenses.summary: Reopening does not mean the threat has ended: Saudi authorities reported fresh interceptions on October 25, while the Houthis publicly warned airlines and travelers against using the airport. Those are competing stakeholder positions, not a settled safety assessment.

claims.text: Saudi coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and drone aimed toward Riyadh early on October 25.
Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said King Khalid Airport remained a military target and urged airlines, staff, and travelers not to use it.
Saudi Civil Defense said debris from intercepted Houthi ballistic missiles injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles in Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah on October 25.
Forecast: Riyadh air traffic is likely to remain constrained while missile and drone attacks continue, as Reuters reported minimal traffic immediately after reopening and ongoing Houthi threats.

story_report.summary: Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport is reopening after a two-week shutdown prompted by repeated Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, but the return of service is partial and subject to security risks. From October 25, Terminal 1 was assigned to domestic flights and Terminal 2 to international flights operated by Saudi national carriers. The airport told passengers with confirmed bookings to check with airlines before travelling, while flight-tracking data reported by Reuters showed little traffic immediately after the announced reopening.

sections.heading: Airport attacks caused casualties and damage
sections.body: Saudi Arabia’s General Authority of Civil Aviation said an October 8 attack struck airport facilities and a Saudia aircraft, killing three Saudi citizens, injuring others and causing material damage. It said a further October 11 attack caused injuries and required continued assessments of damage and facility safety alongside security agencies. Reuters reported that the Saudi-led coalition said Houthis carried out 20 attacks on the airport between October 1 and October 11.

sections.heading: Houthi threats challenge Riyadh operations
sections.body: Saudi coalition spokesman Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said air defenses intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile and drone aimed toward Riyadh early on October 25. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said King Khalid Airport remained a military target and urged airlines, staff and travelers not to use it. Saudi Civil Defense said debris from intercepted missiles injured two people and damaged residential buildings and vehicles in Khamis Mushait and Ahad Rafidah that day.

sections.heading: Full service restoration remains uncertain
sections.body: Available reporting does not establish when all terminals, international carriers or the full range of airport services will resume normal operations. Continued missile and drone threats, alongside minimal traffic immediately after the partial reopening, suggest air traffic is likely to remain constrained. No public source consulted provides a reliable timetable either for an end to the attacks or for full restoration of airport operations.

related_stories.title: Israel Implements Restrictions in West Bank Ahead of Elections Following Soldier Deaths
related_stories.summary: In the lead-up to elections, Israel has announced the closure of all land crossings between Israel and the West Bank on election day. This decision follows a deadly attack in Hebron that resulted in the deaths of two Israeli soldiers. Concurrently, Israeli military operations have led to the displacement of approximately 1,200 Palestinians from their homes in Hebron, as part of a broader crackdown in response to the attack.

related_stories.title: Rescue Efforts Underway After Nairobi Building Collapse Leaves Five Missing
related_stories.summary: A multi-storey building in Nairobi collapsed while still under construction, resulting in two people being rescued and five others reported missing. Police have initiated a manhunt for the building's owner and contractor. Additionally, police used tear gas to disperse crowds and looters at the scene.
